newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-YEBOAH TO QUIT IF LEEDS PROBLEMS CONTINUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-YEBOAH TO QUIT IF LEEDS PROBLEMS CONTINUE.

text.p: Leeds United's troubled striker Tony Yeboah is threatening to quit soccer and return to his native Ghana if he fails to solve his problems with manager George Graham at the English premier league club.

Sources close to the player said on Tuesday that the 31-year-old Yeboah had not turned up for recent pre-season training because he wanted to know if he had a future at the club or whether Graham was willing to let him leave.

Yeboah, who joined Leeds from German club Eintracht Frankfurt during the 1994-5 season, does not get on with the Leeds manager and is not prepared to spend another season at the northern club if he cannot get first-team football.
"Tony is very frustrated. He has the impression that he could play like a World Cup star and he would still have no chance with Graham," one source told Reuters.

"He doesn't want to spend the next season watching from the stands or playing in the reserves. He is seriously thinking of packing it all in and going back to Ghana rather than do that. What he wants is for Leeds to make it clear what the situation is."

Yeboah's contract is due to run until the end of July 1998. A handful of clubs have shown an interest in buying the striker, including three from the Bundesliga where he enjoyed a successful time at Eintracht before he left under a cloud after a dispute with the coach.
"There are no firm offers there yet. But people don't know how much he would cost," the source said. "He wants to continue playing football but he needs Leeds to make their position clear."
Yeboah went through a turbulent time last season. At one point he was fined two weeks' pay after ripping off his shirt and throwing it at Graham after being substituted during a league match.
Yeboah is now unlikely to appear at training for next month's start to the season until he sees some progress in his situation.
Leeds were reported on Tuesday to be ready to let one or two players leave the club. But no leading officials were available to confirm the report.
